question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> be a point in the first octant, whose image <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> in the plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (that is, the line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> is perpendicular to the plane <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and the mid-point of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> lies in the plane <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>) lies on the z-axis. Let the distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> from the x-axis be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the image of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> in the xy-plane, then the length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>R</mi></math> is ______.

solution.text:
Let Pα,β,γ, Q0,0,γ and Rα,β,-γ
Now, PQ→∥i^+j^ ⇒-αi^+βj^∥i^+j^
⇒α=β
Also, mid point of PQ lies on the plane
⇒α2+β2=3⇒α+β=6⇒α=3
Now, distance of point P from x-axis is β2+γ2=5
⇒β2+γ2=25⇒γ2=16
As β=α=3
As γ=4
Hence, PR=2γ=8
